editorial_reason: Inspected Stacks Schemes 26.9 Definition 26.9.1. It identifies schemes as locally ringed spaces with a neighbourhood basis of affine schemes and morphisms as locally ringed-space morphisms.

definitions.text: A scheme is a locally ringed space (X,O_X) in which every point admits an open neighbourhood isomorphic, as a locally ringed space, to Spec(R) with its structure sheaf for some commutative ring R.
A morphism of schemes is a morphism of locally ringed spaces: a continuous map f:X→Y together with a compatible sheaf homomorphism O_Y→f_*O_X inducing local ring homomorphisms on stalks.

definitions.text: The interior Int_X(A) of a subset A of a topological space X is the union of all open subsets of X contained in A, equivalently the largest open subset of X lying in A.
